==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|full-stop|fullstop}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˌfʊl ˈstɒp/|a=RP}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-full stop.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|EN-AU ck1 full stop.ogg|a=AU}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|UK|Ireland|Commonwealth}} The [[punctuation mark]] ⟨'''{{l|mul|.}}'''⟩ (indicating the end of a sentence or marking an abbreviation).
#* {{quote-book|1=en |author={{w|Sarah Kane}} |title={{w|4.48 Psychosis}} |publisher={{w|Methuen Publishing|Methuen}} |year=2002 |isbn=0-413-74830-8 |page=41 |pages=|text=the final period / the final '''full stop'''}}
# {{lb|en|figurative}} A [[decisive]] [[end]] to something.
#* {{RQ:Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2022/oct/22/its-a-way-to-bring-my-mum-and-dad-back-steven-spielberg-on-the-new-wave-of-cine-memoirs|title=‘It’s a way to bring my mum and dad back’: Steven Spielberg on the new wave of cine-memoirs|date=2022-10-22|author=Wendy Ide|quotee=Steven Spielberg|passage=[S]pielberg was keen to stress that ''The Fabelmans'' is not a '''full stop''': “It is not because I decided to retire, and this is my swan song, don’t believe that.”}}
# A [[complete]] [[stop]].
#* {{RQ:NYT|date=26 February 1978|author=Richard F. Shepard|title=ABOUT LONG ISLAND: 7 Hours to Manhasset, and So Forth|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/xLGo2|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1978/02/26/archives/long-island-weekly-about-long-island-7-hours-to-manhasset-and-so.html|archivedate=10 December 2025|passage=The train moved slowly, very slowly, but at least it was moving, and the customers were grateful even for indecisive motion going their way. Just outside the Nassau border, in Queens, the train came to a '''full stop'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Independent|date=3 December 2018|author=Chris Riotta|title=How police stopped a speeding Tesla with a sleeping driver behind the wheel|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20181204085613/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/tesla-autopilot-police-speeding-sleeping-driver-california-steering-wheel-a8665811.html|passage=What’s more, Mr Samek did not even wake up after the car had come to a '''full stop''': officers were forced to wake hm up by knocking on the window, according to a police report that indicated the autopilot feature was likely on “considering the vehicle’s ability to slow to a stop when Samek was asleep.” }}
#* {{RQ:Observer|date=27 March 2022|author=Laurie Clarke|title=How self-driving cars got stuck in the slow lane|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220327131040/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2022/mar/27/how-self-driving-cars-got-stuck-in-the-slow-lane|passage=For example, the NHTSA forced Tesla to prevent the system from executing illegal “rolling stops” (moving slowly through a stop sign without ever coming to a '''full stop''', while an “unexpected braking” problem is the subject of a current inquiry.}}
